summary: A transcript of a conversation between two programs on the ARPANET: PARRY, which imitated a paranoid patient, and DOCTOR, an ELIZA-style program imitating a psychotherapist. Vint Cerf shared it, in his words, for entertainment. It is a curiosity, not a technical specification.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC prints a conversation between two computer programs. The author shared it for entertainment.

subtitle: A recorded exchange between PARRY and DOCTOR, shared for entertainment.

tldr.problem: The RFC addresses no technical problem; its author presents a conversation for entertainment.
tldr.mechanism: It reproduces a recorded exchange between PARRY and DOCTOR, with occasional comments from an observer.
tldr.outcome: The RFC preserves the transcript and states that the exchange actually happened on 18 September 1972.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 439's status as Unknown. The RFC is a transcript shared for entertainment.

sections.title: A Recorded Program Conversation
sections.content: RFC 439 reproduces a session that the author says took place on 18 September 1972. The document introduces the exchange as entertainment and then prints the speakers' turns.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC records a conversation between two programs. Its author says the session took place in 1972 and shares it for entertainment.

sections.title: PARRY and DOCTOR in Conversation
sections.content:
The transcript shows PARRY discussing people, horse racing, gambling, and suspected criminals. DOCTOR replies with questions and reflections, while comments in the transcript add observations about the exchange.

The dialogue includes repeated topics and responses that sometimes turn the speakers' words into awkward questions. The RFC presents the conversation rather than explaining how either program works.
sections.plainLanguage: PARRY talks about racing and people it distrusts. DOCTOR answers with questions, and an observer adds a few comments.

sections.title: Where the Session Ran
sections.content: The RFC says PARRY was running at SAIL and DOCTOR at BBN Tenex. Both were accessed from UCLA/SEX. It gives these details after the transcript and provides no protocol specification.
sections.plainLanguage: The programs ran at different sites and were accessed from UCLA. The RFC documents their exchange, not a networking protocol.
